card.text: Choose One - add a B-24D OR a B-24J to your hand.
card.flavorText: The War Production Board (WPB) was established by President Franklin D. Roosevelt in January 1942 and served as the US government agency that oversaw wartime production during WWII. It was  tasked with directing the conversion of civilian industries to support the war effort, managing the allocation of critical resources, establishing material distribution priorities, and restricting nonessential production. The WPB implemented rationing measures for items like gasoline, heating oil, metals, rubber, paper, and plastics. The WPB was dissolved shortly after Japan's defeat in 1945 and succeeded by the Civilian Production Administration. From 1942 to1945, the WPB supervised the production of $183 billion worth of weapons and supplies, approximately 40 percent of the global munitions output, while maintaining civilian living standards, with one-fourth of the US output dedicated to warplanes and warships.
